title: Strong edge colouring with maximum degree 4: 20 or 21 colours?
premise_risks: A 2026 improvement to 20 might exist that the searches missed
plain: A strong edge colouring gives edges colours so that any two edges that touch, or are joined by a third edge, get different colours. Erdős and Nešetřil conjectured that graphs with maximum degree 4 need at most 20 colours; it is proved that 21 suffice. Close the one-colour gap.
math: Prove that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\le4$ has strong chromatic index $\chi'_s(G)\le20$ (Erdos-Nesetril bound $\tfrac54\Delta^2$), or find a graph with $\Delta\le4$ and $\chi'_s=21$.
review_note: Known: chi'_s <= 22: Cranston (2006, arXiv:math/0601623). chi'_s <= 21: Huang-Santana-Yu, Electron. J. Combin. 25(3) (2018) P3.31 (arXiv:1806.07012). Lower bound 20 is attained by the blow-up of C_5 (each vertex replaced by 2 vertices). Related: packing edge-colouring results for Delta <= 4 (Involve 18(2), 2025) do not give 20. Delta=3 is settled (10; Andersen, Horak-He-Trotter).
